transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been worried about how I eat at night. Once I start picking at food, I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then my hand just keeps going back. It feels like I’m not really the one making the decision anymore.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started, even if you want to?

Yes. That’s the part that worries me. Once I start picking at food late at night, I’ll tell myself, like, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then my hand keeps going back anyway. It feels like I’m not really the one deciding anymore.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during these late-night episodes?

Not really, no. That’s what bothers me. I’ll be there late at night, just picking at food, and I’ll tell myself, enough, Santiago, stop now. But then I keep reaching for more anyway, like I’m not the one making the choice.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these late-night eating episodes?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t feel good about it, but I don’t know if I’d call it guilt or shame exactly. I just kind of feel bothered afterward, like, “Why did I do that again?”
Do you feel like these late-night eating episodes are causing you a lot of stress or anxiety?
I don’t know if I’d say a lot of stress or anxiety. It bothers me, yeah, and I think about it after, but I haven’t really noticed it making me anxious like that.
Do you think you're eating a large amount of food during these late-night episodes?

Yeah, I think so. Some nights after work, I’ll go through several tamales, then maybe a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left. It’s like I’m standing there in the kitchen telling myself I’m just cleaning up leftovers, but it ends up being a lot.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating during these episodes because you can't control your eating, or is it more that you just keep deciding to have a little more?
It feels more like I can’t control it once I get started. I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then I keep reaching for more anyway, like the decision’s already out of my hands.
Do you feel like you're eating really quickly during these late-night episodes?

Yeah, I do. I eat a lot faster than I would if I was sitting down with my family. It’s more like I’m trying to hurry up and get it over with before anyone wakes up, and sometimes I’m barely even tasting it.
Do you ever have episodes like this during the day, or is it only at night?
I’m not really sure. I’ve noticed it more at night, that’s when it stands out to me. During the day I’m usually busy, so if it happens, I don’t pay attention to it the same way.
Do you usually try to eat these late-night meals alone, without others knowing?
Yeah. I usually wait until my aunt and everybody else is asleep. I don’t like them seeing how much I’m eating, so I try to be quiet in the kitchen and keep it to myself.
Has this nighttime eating behavior interfered with your daily life or relationships in any way?

A little bit, yeah. I’m still making it to my shipping and receiving shifts and taking care of what I need to do. But at home, I’ve started avoiding being in the kitchen with family later at night. I get worried they’ll notice how uncomfortable I am around the food, so I kind of keep my distance.
Do you think this nighttime eating is affecting your overall well-being or how you feel about yourself?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t feel great about it afterward, and I don’t like that I hide it. But I don’t know if I’d say it’s affecting my whole well-being. It mostly just makes me feel kind of disappointed in myself.
Do you eat at night because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating and don't want others to see it?
Yeah, pretty much. I get embarrassed by how much I can eat, so I wait until my aunt and everyone else is asleep. Then I try to be quiet in the kitchen so nobody notices.
Do you feel like you're eating in secret at night because you're embarrassed about the amount of food you're consuming?
Yeah, that’s basically it. I don’t like anyone seeing how much I’m eating, so I wait until my aunt and the rest of the house are asleep. Then I try to keep quiet in the kitchen.
Do you think this nighttime eating behavior is significantly affecting your ability to function or causing you a lot of distress?

It’s distressing, yeah, but I’m still making it to my shipping and receiving shifts and getting my responsibilities done. I wouldn’t say it’s stopping me from functioning. The main thing is I’ve started avoiding being in the kitchen with family later at night because I’m worried someone will notice how uncomfortable I get around the food.
Do you feel like you're no longer in control of your eating during these episodes?

Yeah. That’s the part that bothers me. Once I start picking at food late at night, I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then my hand just keeps going back. It feels like I’m not really the one deciding anymore.
Do you usually feel anxious, stressed, or upset right before these late-night eating episodes?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that. Sometimes I’m just up late and I end up in the kitchen, but I can’t say it’s always because I’m anxious or upset right before.
Do you feel uncomfortably full after these late-night eating episodes?
Yeah, I do. By the time I stop, my stomach feels really tight and heavy. I usually have to sit on the edge of the couch for a while, because if I bend over or try to lie down, it feels pretty bad.
Do you think you usually eat at night because you're feeling emotional, like stressed, anxious, or upset?
I don’t really know. I can’t say I’ve noticed that it’s because I’m stressed or upset. Sometimes it’s just late, I’m awake, and I end up eating.
